title: CI/CD Automation with GitHub Actions & Azure OIDC
description: Architect enterprise continuous integration and continuous delivery pipelines using GitHub Actions, OIDC passwordless authentication, and automated quality gates.

data.text: Automated Delivery for Enterprise .NET & React AI

In a fast-moving AI product team, delivering updates reliably requires a fully automated CI/CD pipeline. Every commit must be automatically compiled, tested with unit and prompt evaluation suites, scanned for container CVEs, and published to Azure without human intervention. Crucially, modern enterprise pipelines eliminate static service principal passwords by using OpenID Connect (OIDC) federated credentials.
Passwordless Azure Authentication with OpenID Connect (OIDC)

Rather than storing long-lived Azure client secrets in GitHub repository secrets (which can leak or expire without warning), OIDC issues short-lived, cryptographically signed JWT tokens directly from GitHub to Azure Entra ID, verifying repository and branch identity on the fly.

data.title: Production GitHub Actions Pipeline with OIDC and Evaluation Gates
data.content: A complete CI/CD workflow building .NET, running tests, and deploying to Azure:
data.code:
name: CI/CD Pipeline - .NET & React AI Platform

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

permissions:
  id-token: write # Required for requesting Azure OIDC JWT token
  contents: read

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Setup .NET SDK
      uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
      with:
        dotnet-version: '9.0.x'

    - name: Restore dependencies
      run: dotnet restore

    - name: Build solution
      run: dotnet build --no-restore -c Release

    - name: Run Unit Tests & Quality Benchmarks
      run: dotnet test --no-build -c Release --verbosity normal --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"

  deploy-staging:
    needs: build-and-test
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Azure Login via OIDC
      uses: azure/login@v2
      with:
        client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
        tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
        subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}

    - name: Build & Push Container to ACR
      run: |
        az acr login --name acrlearnai
        docker build -t acrlearnai.azurecr.io/learnai-api:${{ github.sha }} -f Dockerfile .
        docker push acrlearnai.azurecr.io/learnai-api:${{ github.sha }}

    - name: Deploy to Azure App Service Staging Slot
      uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
      with:
        app-name: 'app-learnai-api'
        slot-name: 'staging'
        images: 'acrlearnai.azurecr.io/learnai-api:${{ github.sha }}'

Health check 200 OK and test chat stream succeeds

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Automate the entire delivery lifecycle from commit to production with GitHub Actions
Use Azure OpenID Connect (OIDC) to eliminate stored passwords and static service principal secrets
Incorporate automated AI evaluation gates into CI to block prompt and model regressions
Deploy container images tagged with immutable Git commit SHAs for auditable provenance
Deploy to staging slots and run automated smoke tests before swapping to production
data.takeaway: Enterprise CI/CD brings software engineering discipline to AI. Combining OIDC security, container automation, and evaluation quality gates ensures reliable, fearless production releases.
